title: Ukrainian special forces strike Syzran oil refinery and Atlant Aero drone plant; refinery halts operations
detail: Ukraine's Special Operations Forces, working with the Unmanned Systems Forces and the Security Service of Ukraine, struck Rosneft's Syzran oil refinery in Samara region overnight on Sept 14-15, hitting the AVT-6 (CDU-6) primary crude distillation unit — 71% of the plant's total processing capacity — and its tank farm, sparking fires. The refinery's smaller CDU-5 unit (29% of capacity) was already offline for repairs from a July strike, so the new hit left the 8.9-million-tonne/year plant with no functioning primary distillation capacity; industry sources told Reuters the refinery halted operations on Sept 15, with repairs to the AVT-6 unit expected to take at least a month. The same overnight wave also struck the Atlant Aero drone-production facility in Taganrog, Rostov region, which manufactures Molniya strike-reconnaissance drones and components for Orion UAVs supplying Russian forces; a large fire was reported there. No casualties were reported at either site. Syzran and the already-halted Saratov refinery (down since Sept 11) together represent about 290,000 barrels/day of combined processing capacity now offline.

title: Reuters: 3 of Russia's 6 largest diesel refineries now curbed or halted by drone strikes
detail: Reuters reported that three of Russia's six largest diesel-producing refineries — Omsk, Kirishi, Taneco, Volgograd, NORSI and Perm together account for roughly half of national diesel output — are now either shut or running at a fraction of capacity after September's drone campaign. Kirishi (KINEF) remains completely offline (halted since Sept 2); Volgograd and NORSI are each running at about 25% of nameplate capacity; Taneco, struck overnight Sept 12-13, has damage still being assessed. Diesel output at the affected plants is running several times below normal, and combined diesel/gasoil exports have fallen to roughly 1.8 million tonnes a month, down from a typical 2.5-3.4 million tonnes. The IEA said a Russian refinery has been successfully hit on average once every three days over the first eight months of 2026, part of a campaign of at least 70 confirmed strikes on refineries since January that has pushed refining output to its lowest level in two decades.

title: Leningrad Oblast caps fuel purchases at 30 liters as Kirishi refinery remains offline
detail: Leningrad Oblast will introduce a uniform 30-liter (about 8-gallon) per-fill-up purchase cap at gas stations in the coming days, the regional government said, after oil companies proposed the limit amid the continued shutdown of the Kirishi (KINEF) refinery — the region's largest fuel supplier. Governor Alexander Drozdenko called the measure temporary, running through Oct 1, and said the top priority was 'preventing panic,' which fuels a surge in demand. He said about 20% of independent and small gas stations had stopped operating because they could not buy the volumes they needed on the commodities exchange. AI-92 gasoline supply is 'stabilizing,' Drozdenko said, but AI-95 remains tight, while the region has no diesel shortage. Emergency vehicles are exempt from the cap.
